documentation-index.notes: Blockquote directing readers to the documentation index llms.txt. Navigation/meta only.

how-claude-code-works.notes: H1 + subtitle. Scope: agentic loop, built-in tools, how Claude Code interacts with a project.

claude-code-is-an-agentic-assistant.notes: Opening paragraph: Claude Code runs in terminal; handles coding and anything doable from the command line. Pointers to Common workflows and Extend Claude Code.

the-agentic-loop.notes: H2: Three phases — gather context, take action, verify results.

agentic-loop-diagram.notes: Diagram of the agentic loop: prompt -> gather -> act -> verify -> repeat, with user interrupt available at any point.

the-loop-adapts.notes: The loop scales to task complexity. Claude chains dozens of actions and course-corrects. User can interrupt at any point.

agentic-loop-powered-by.notes: Loop powered by models (reason) and tools (act). Claude Code is the agentic harness: provides tools, context management, execution environment around the language model.

models.notes: H3: Claude models reason about code and tasks. Multiple models available with different tradeoffs. Sonnet for most tasks; Opus for complex architectural decisions. Switch with `/model` or `claude --model <name>`.

tools.notes: H3: Tools make Claude Code agentic — without tools, only text output. Each tool use returns information feeding back into the loop.

built-in-tools-table.notes: Five built-in tool categories: file operations, search, execution, web, code intelligence. Code intelligence requires code intelligence plugins.

tools-also-subagents.notes: Claude also has tools for spawning subagents, asking questions, and other orchestration tasks. Links to Tools reference for complete list.

tool-use-example.notes: Example sequence for 'fix the failing tests': run suite, read error, search source, read files, edit, run again. Demonstrates agentic loop in action.

extending-base-capabilities.notes: Built-in tools are foundation; extend with skills, MCP, hooks, subagents. These form a layer on top of core agentic loop.

what-claude-can-access.notes: H2: Focuses on terminal. Claude Code also runs in VS Code, JetBrains, other environments.

what-claude-can-access-list.notes: Access list: project files, terminal (any CLI command), git state, CLAUDE.md, auto memory (first 200 lines or 25KB of MEMORY.md), configured extensions (MCP, skills, subagents, Claude in Chrome).

because-claude-sees-your-whole-project.notes: Full-project access enables cross-file coordination: search, multi-file edit, test, commit. Contrasted with inline code assistants that only see the current file.

environments-and-interfaces.notes: H2: Agentic loop is the same everywhere; what changes is where code executes and how you interact.

execution-environments.notes: H3: Three execution environments — Local (default, full access), Cloud (Anthropic-managed VMs), Remote Control (local machine controlled from browser).

execution-environments-table.notes: Table: Local, Cloud, Remote Control — where code runs and use case for each.

interfaces.notes: H3: Terminal, desktop app, IDE extensions, claude.ai/code, Remote Control, Slack, CI/CD pipelines. Interface changes interaction but not the underlying agentic loop.

work-with-sessions.notes: H2: Conversations saved locally as JSONL under ~/.claude/projects/. Enables rewind, resume, fork. Files snapshotted before edits. Sessions are independent — fresh context window each time.

sessions-are-independent.notes: Each new session = fresh context window. Auto memory and CLAUDE.md persist learnings across sessions.

work-across-branches.notes: H3: Sessions tied to current directory. Branch switch = Claude sees new files, conversation history unchanged. Parallel sessions via git worktrees (separate directories).

resume-or-fork-sessions.notes: H3: `--continue` / `--resume` uses same session ID, appends messages, restores conversation history but NOT session-scoped permissions (must re-approve). `--fork-session` creates new session ID preserving history — original unchanged. Forked sessions also don't inherit session-scoped permissions.

same-session-multiple-terminals.notes: Caveat: resuming the same session in multiple terminals interleaves writes to the same file. Nothing corrupts but conversation becomes jumbled. Use `--fork-session` for parallel work from same starting point.

the-context-window.notes: H3: Context holds conversation history, file contents, command outputs, CLAUDE.md, auto memory, loaded skills, system instructions. Claude compacts automatically; early instructions can get lost. Use CLAUDE.md for persistent rules, `/context` to inspect usage.

when-context-fills-up.notes: H4: Auto compaction order: clears older tool outputs first, then summarizes. Requests and key code preserved; early detailed instructions may be lost. `/compact` accepts a focus argument. Thrashing error if single file/output refills context immediately — stops auto-compacting after a few attempts.

mcp-deferred-context.notes: MCP tool definitions deferred by default (tool search). Only tool names consume context until a specific tool is used. `/mcp` checks per-server costs.

manage-context-with-skills-and-subagents.notes: H4: Skills load on demand (descriptions at start, full content when used). `disable-model-invocation: true` keeps descriptions out until invoked. Subagents get own fresh context — work doesn't bloat main session, returns summary. Isolation is why subagents help with long sessions.

stay-safe-with-checkpoints-and-permissio.notes: H2: Two safety mechanisms — checkpoints (undo file changes) and permissions (control what Claude can do without asking).

undo-changes-with-checkpoints.notes: H3: Every file edit reversible — Claude snapshots file before editing. Esc twice to rewind. Checkpoints are local to session, separate from git, cover file changes only. Caveat: remote actions (databases, APIs, deployments) can't be checkpointed.

control-what-claude-can-do.notes: H3: Shift+Tab cycles permission modes — Default (asks for edits and commands), Auto-accept edits, Plan mode (read-only, generates plan), Auto mode (background safety checks, research preview). Specific commands allowable in `.claude/settings.json`. Settings can be scoped organization-wide to personal.

work-effectively-with-claude-code.notes: H2 section: Tips for better results. Divider separates core mechanics from usage guidance.

ask-claude-code-for-help.notes: H3: Claude Code can explain itself. Built-in commands: /init (create CLAUDE.md), /agents (configure subagents), /doctor (diagnose issues).

its-a-conversation.notes: H3: No need for perfect prompts. Start with intent, refine through iteration.

conversation-example.notes: Example exchange: initial prompt -> Claude tries -> user correction -> Claude adjusts. No need to start over.

interrupt-and-steer.notes: H4: Can interrupt Claude at any point by typing a correction and pressing Enter. Claude stops and adjusts immediately.

be-specific-upfront.notes: H3: Precise prompts with file references, constraints, patterns succeed on first attempt. Vague prompts require more steering.

be-specific-example.notes: Example specific prompt: references src/payments/, mentions token refresh, specifies test-first approach.

give-claude-something-to-verify-against.notes: H3: Claude performs better with verifiable success criteria — test cases, screenshots, expected output. Run tests after. For visual work, paste a screenshot.

explore-before-implementing.notes: H3: Separate research from coding. Plan mode (Shift+Tab twice) for read-only analysis. Two-phase approach: plan first, implement second.

delegate-dont-dictate.notes: H3: Give context and direction; let Claude determine the steps. Don't need to specify which files to read or commands to run.

whats-next.notes: H2: Card group navigation — Extend with features, Common workflows. Navigation only.
